chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Ray Charles leaves and takes Cooper and Fathead
summary: Ray later sent for Cooper and Fathead for his big band; Smith's time with Ray was only weeks or months.

bands.name: Doug Finley and the Sanctified Fire

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Tell me, how long did you continue to work with Ray Charles?
Ray? It wasn't too long. Because he finally left here.
Did he want you to go with him?
No. He knew I wasn't going to go with him. No. He just went on out there by himself.
He went to Seattle.

Yeah, went around back up there somewhere. Then his agent got (?) and booked some more dates for him, and he sent for me and told me he wanted to make a big band or something or other. He first started with eight pieces, made up of eight pieces. So we sent and got Cooper and Fathead out from under me.
Were they working with you in the band here?
Yeah.
You must have missed them.
Yeah, I sure missed them. Sure did.
Because they're two really good men.
Yeah. Of course, Fathead never did play on the
Buster Smith - 198

records with him, but Cooper did. Let me see, Fathead was playng with another little old band around here called Doug Finley and the Sanctified Fire. A friend of mine, a trumpet player -- an old trumpet player.
Why couldn't you get him for that record you made with...?
He was with somebody else.
But it was only a recording date. Couldn't you have got him for the record?
Yeah, but he wasn't in town, I don't think. He was out of town. I think he was down in Houston somewhere.
So your time with Ray Charles was just what? A matter of months?
Yeah.
Or weeks?
